title: Social Capital and Innovation: Evidence from Facebook Friendship Networks
discussion_signal: The co-author summarizes that one standard deviation higher economic connectedness is associated with 97% more patents per capita among patenting ZIP Codes and 45% more breakthrough patents per capita among ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents. The post also says complementary designs support a causal interpretation and that mechanism tests are consistent with financing as one channel. This gives the industrial innovation story a bounded public translation: cross-class networks may affect who gets exposure to financing and opportunity, not merely whether a place has social cohesion.
linked_research_question: Through which financing, information, and inventor-mobility channels could economic connectedness change U.S. industrial innovation, and where might the Facebook-network measure fail to represent firms, workers, or consumers?
limits: The post is a short co-author summary and does not provide the paper's full tables, sample construction, or uncertainty intervals
The estimates are conditional on patenting ZIP Codes and do not establish a universal effect for all U.S. communities or firms
Economic connectedness is not the same as trust, institutional quality, financing received, firm survival, worker outcomes, or consumer welfare
A single LinkedIn post is not representative of inventors, firms, households, or policymakers
